samples.summary: New confirmation gate on `GET /auth/github?mode=cli` changes a contract that already-released CLI builds depend on
samples.evidence: The middleware now answers `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=…` with an HTML page instead of a 302 to GitHub (packages/backend/src/auth/cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:65-108). The in-tree CLI was updated for this (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:35-46 + 180s timeout), but any previously installed/published `wafflebase` CLI opens the same URL and waits only 30 s with no notice that a click is required (the old `setTimeout(..., 30_000)` this diff replaces). Those clients now have to fit a confirmation click *plus* the whole GitHub sign-in into 30 s, and a headless copy-paste user is even less likely to make it. Nothing in the repo pins the backend↔CLI compatibility direction of old-CLI/new-backend (the diff only handles new-CLI/old-backend, via REFUSAL.noState). Fix likely belongs on the backend: keep the gate but make it explicit in the release notes / consider tolerating a nonce-less legacy CLI faster path.

samples.summary: `__Host-`/`Secure` state cookie makes every browser login unrecoverable on documented plain-HTTP production deployments
samples.evidence: `isSecureCookie()` keys purely off `NODE_ENV === 'production'` (packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:117) and the cookie name becomes `__Host-wafflebase_oauth_state`, which browsers only accept over HTTPS. Self-hosting is documented with plain-HTTP production URLs — `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL=http://localhost:3000/auth/github/callback` and `FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost:5173` (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42-43) and `http://your-domain:3000/auth/github/callback` (self-hosting.md:121). On such an install the state cookie is silently dropped, so `webOAuthStateMatches` always fails and `githubAuthCallback` redirects to `/login?error=oauth_state` on every attempt — a login loop with no session, where before the change login completed (the pre-existing `secure` session cookies degraded, but did not block sign-in). Fix belongs on the new code: derive `secure` from the request/`FRONTEND_URL` scheme rather than NODE_ENV, or document the HTTPS requirement.

samples.summary: User-facing CLI docs still describe the old login flow (no confirmation click, no `oauth_state` refusal)
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:25 still says only "The CLI opens your browser for GitHub authentication and stores the JWT session". The new required step — the backend answers with a confirmation page the user must click through, and the CLI now prints "Confirm the sign-in in the browser to continue." plus refusal diagnostics (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:43-46, 200-230) — is documented only in docs/design/cli.md:168-240 and packages/backend/README.md. The user-facing consumer of that contract was left describing the previous behaviour.

samples.summary: CLI confirmation gate is bound to a hard-coded route string and a hard-coded href; a mount-path/global-prefix change silently degrades CLI login instead of failing loudly
samples.evidence: The gate is registered as `.forRoutes({ path: 'auth/github', method: RequestMethod.GET })` (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.module.ts:48) and the Continue link is the literal `/auth/github?…` (packages/backend/src/auth/cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:126). `GitHubAuthGuard` mints CLI state only when `req.__cliConfirmed` is set (packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:57), so if the middleware ever stops matching the route (a `setGlobalPrefix`, a reverse-proxy sub-path mount, a controller path rename) every `wafflebase login` silently degrades to a browser login and the CLI hangs until its timeout, with no error anywhere. `packages/backend/src/main.ts` sets no global prefix today, but other controllers already live under `api/v1` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts), so the two spellings of the path are an invariant nothing enforces.

verdict.reason: The described code is real (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:66-109 answers GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=… with a 200 HTML confirmation page, and github-auth.guard.ts:57-62 mints CLI state only for a confirmed request), but it is not a blocking blast-radius defect. (1) No in-repo consumer is broken or bypassing: grepping `mode=cli` across the tree finds only packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:40 (updated with the confirm notice and a 180s wait at login.ts:43-46,188), the backend files/specs, and docs that were all updated (docs/design/cli.md:176-243, packages/backend/README.md:184,410, docs/design/rest-api.md:334). The only "unupdated caller" the finding names is a previously-published @wafflebase/cli npm artifact (packages/cli/package.json), i.e. not a location in this repository that needs to change, and the reviewer's own remedy is release notes rather than a code fix. (2) The legacy client shape was in fact considered and is tolerated end to end: the confirm page omits the nonce when absent (middleware:123-126), parseCliNonce may be undefined (guard:16-19,60), and the loopback redirect appends `&state=` only when a nonce exists (auth.controller.ts:178-183), so a nonce-less legacy CLI still completes the flow. (3) Residual impact is a client-side timeout with an actionable retry message (login.ts:215-218) — no data loss, no crash, no guard bypass — which under this lens's severity scale is at most minor ("a consumer that still works but is now inconsistent"), and the repo already documents the backend/CLI version coupling at docs/design/cli.md:211-212.

Self-hosting is documented with plain-HTTP production URLs — `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL=http://localhost:3000/auth/github/callback` and `FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost:5173` (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42-43) and `http://your-domain:3000/auth/github/callback` (self-hosting.md:121). verdict.reason: Verified independently. isSecureCookie() keys solely off NODE_ENV === 'production' (oauth-state.ts:116-118) with no request/scheme input, producing __Host-wafflebase_oauth_state + Secure (oauth-state.ts:60-62, :102). The callback reads only the currently-minted cookie name and, on mismatch, redirects to /login?error=oauth_state without issuing a session (auth.controller.ts:156-164), so a dropped cookie is an unrecoverable login loop, not a degraded login. The scenario is reachable and documented: Dockerfile:88 hard-sets NODE_ENV=production, while self-hosting.md:42-43 and :121 document plain-HTTP production URLs, and a grep of packages/documentation found no HTTPS/TLS/reverse-proxy requirement. No guard elsewhere can override the flag; hostPrefixedCookieName is consumed on the same terms by cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:50. The one plausible refutation - that pre-existing Secure session cookies (auth.controller.ts:327) already broke plain-HTTP production login so nothing new breaks - does not hold at high confidence, because the documented URLs are http://localhost, a trustworthy origin where browsers do accept Secure cookies, while __Host- acceptance over a non-https scheme is browser-dependent and unverifiable from this repo. In lane: a new precondition that existing deployment artifacts and documented configs outside the diff do not supply, breaking a consumer path the diff does not show.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason:
This is not a code finding at all — it is a report that the blast-radius reviewer process itself terminated without a verdict because the review harness's API credential pool was exhausted. It names no file, no symbol, no changed contract, and no bypassing call site, so there is nothing in the repository that matches "a new guard with a bypass", "a changed contract with unupdated callers", or any other item in the blast-radius lane.

I traced the quoted string to its only source in the tree: `poolExhaustedError()` in scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637 builds exactly the message `"<label>: every credential in the pool (N) was retired — nothing left to fail over to"` and tags it `kind: "pool-exhausted"`, `retryable: false`. The surrounding doc comment (scripts/agent/ask.mjs:607-629) shows this is deliberate, single-source error construction so that the two reachable exhaustion sites (pre-session drain check and the failover loop's last-live-slot retirement) cannot disagree; scripts/agent/ask.mjs:730-739 documents the deliberate decision that a drained pool must fail rather than fall through to the ambient credential. The behaviour is pinned by tests at scripts/agent/ask.test.mjs:302, 321 and 341, and the identical file exists in .trusted/scripts/agent/ask.mjs:632, i.e. it is unchanged, pre-existing, intended behaviour rather than a defect.

The repository even records this exact operational outcome as a known infrastructure failure mode distinct from a completed review: docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-lessons.md:276-285 describes a prior round where a lens "ran its full ~14 minutes and produced no findings and no verdict; its summary read 'every credential in the pool (3) was retired'", and that round's blocking set was worked from the other lenses' output. That matches this finding exactly: label "review", pool size 2.

Grounds: `not-present` — there is no described defective code to evaluate; the only code bearing the quoted text is an intentional, tested error message, not a bug. A harness credential exhaustion cannot be fixed in the branch under review and does not belong on the merge gate as a blast-radius defect. (Note: I found no prompt-injection or reviewer-steering text in the files I read; the docs entry above is a neutral retrospective note.)
